thread:
Liam: Heads up — seeing a cluster of ECC / Xid spikes in us-west-2 this morning. ~20 cards reported transient Xid 13 over the last 2h, a few of them flapping. Thinking we should (1) add a short-term grafana panel to track per-card Xid/ECC bursts, (2) soften the ejection curve to avoid mass drains, and (3) flag suspected 'flaky' cards for manual triage. Anyone else seeing this?

Maya: Can you paste the prom query and the error sample? Curious if this is tied to a specific AMI or kernel.

Liam: Quick PromQL snippet of what I used:

```
sum by(gpu_id, region) (increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[15m]))
```

Example log from node-uw2-17:
```
[2026-03-18T08:12:05Z] Xid 13 on GPU 2 (oom/drive timeout) temp=84C, ecc_uncorrected=3
```

Sam: Ugh. Two things we learned from last month: (a) short ECC bursts + high temp often correlate with degraded kernel drivers after hot reboots, (b) immediate ejection makes capacity churn which causes cross-region shifts and transient SLO blips. For healthscore we should add a dampening term: keep a 30m exponential moving average of Xid rate and require sustained > threshold for 3 samples before hard-eject. That reduces false positives. :thinking_face:

Rachel: Also propose a dashboard panel that shows per-card sparkline (last 24h) + a stacked bar for Xid vs ECC vs temperature. We can annotate maintenance windows and past ejections so we see patterns. If we over-eject in us-west-2 we pay for >cross-region fallback and higher tail latency for dedicated customers.

Jon: For SLOs, do we want region-level GPU availability at 99.95% or 99.9%? Right now our regional SLA for Dedicated is 99.9% but we internally target 99.95. If we lower ejection aggressiveness we might need a compensating mitigation like preferring local reboots first.

infra-bot: Alert fired: gpu-xid-rate-high (us-west-2) — 24 instances above warning threshold. See: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/xyz/gpu-health

Maya: Agree with Sam. Also add a 'flaky' label into the node metadata instead of immediate drain. That label prevents scheduler from placing long-lived Dedicated workloads but still allows short test jobs so we can repro. Will add a tag `redwood/gpu:flaky` and include in node exporter metrics.

Liam: Draft of alert rule (RFC):
```
- alert: GPUXidBurst
  expr: increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[15m]) > 5
  for: 30m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU Xid burst in {{ $labels.region }}"
    runbook: "/runbooks/gpu-xid-burst"
```
Notes: set severity=warning for the first firing, escalate to critical only if sustained >1h or if ejection count exceeds 3 in 24h.

Sam: For the healthscore formula, suggestion in pseudocode:
```
health = 100 - clamp( w1*ema(xid_rate,30m) + w2*percent_ecc_uncorrected + w3*temp_excess, 0, 100)
if health < 60 and sustained(30m): mark for manual eject
if health < 40 and sustained(1h): auto-eject
```
where w1=0.6, w2=0.25, w3=0.15 as a starting point. We can tune with historical data.

Rachel: I'll prototype the grafana dashboard (panels: per-card sparkline, region heatmap, ejection timeline) and add the annotations for deploys/AMI changes. Will link the dashboard here when ready. :thumbsup:

Maya: I'll add the node label flow and a short scheduler change to prefer node cordon+soft-drain for flagged nodes. Also agree on lowering automatic ejection aggressiveness.

Liam: Action items: (1) Rachel to push dashboard draft and link (ETA today EOD), (2) Maya to add `redwood/gpu:flaky` label + scheduler soft-drain change (ETA tomorrow), (3) Sam to simulate the dampened healthscore in staging and produce a tuning PR (ETA 2d), (4) Jon to review regional SLO wording if we change ejection policy. I'll update the alert rule to warning-level first.

Jon: Sounds good. If we end up with many flaky nodes we should run an automated remediation job once per week that tries a safe sequence: reboot kernel -> re-run driver verify -> cordon if still bad. Keeps churn controlled.

Liam: Perfect. I'll add the remediation playbook steps to the runbook and tag the incident channel. Thanks everyone :rocket:
